title: How Drummer Abu Kasim Became a Kazi

keywords: how drummer abu kasim became a kazi
full_text:
Abu Kasim was a cheerful festival drummer in the city of Mosul, renowned for his rhythmic precision and his unwavering honesty. While other men flattered wealthy patrons, Abu Kasim played his drum for weddings, harvest fairs, and children's processions, asking only fair wages.

One year, the Sultan of Mosul dismissed his entire judiciary after discovering that the magistrates were accepting golden platters from wealthy litigants.
Frustrated by corruption, the Sultan declared:
'I will appoint no more professional jurists who twist words for profit. I shall find a man whose rhythm in life is pure and incorruptible!'

The Sultan walked disguised through the bazaar and observed a dispute between a wealthy goldsmith and a poor water-carrier. The goldsmith claimed the water-carrier had splashed water on his fine silk coat and demanded ten dinars damages.
Abu Kasim, who was sitting nearby tightening the goatskin of his drum, intervened:
'Wait, neighbor! The coat was splashed by two drops of clean water, which have already dried without leaving a mark. Why charge ten dinars for water that dried into cool air? But since the goldsmith was startled, let the water-carrier give him a cool drink of water, and let the goldsmith give the carrier a copper for his labor!'

The crowd cheered, and both parties departed satisfied.

The Sultan, stepping forward, summoned Abu Kasim to the palace that evening and appointed him Chief Magistrate of the Civil Court!

Abu Kasim protested: 'O King, I know nothing of dusty law volumes; I am only a drummer!'
The Sultan replied: 'A good drummer knows balance, timing, and how to keep every beat true. Apply that rhythm to human affairs.'

On his first day on the bench, a wealthy landholder tried to slip a purse of fifty gold pieces onto Abu Kasim's table to sway a boundary dispute.
Abu Kasim picked up the purse, laid it upon his drum, and beat a furious, deafening rhythm upon the skin!
The coins bounced and jangled loudly across the courtroom floor!
'Listen, citizens!' cried Abu Kasim. 'The gold of corruption makes a hollow, ugly sound! Let the boundaries be measured with honest ropes, not with the jingle of bribes!'

The people cheered Abu Kasim's unbending integrity. For twenty years he served as Kazi, settling disputes with good humor, common sense, and absolute fairness, proving that an upright heart makes the finest magistrate.
moral: Honesty, rhythmic composure, and refusal to accept bribes can elevate the humblest citizen to seats of honor.
